text: He gets his two minutes: husks wall off the passage, everyone runs the drain pipe, and a last line that makes no sense yet.
The worst job goes to her husks: hold, then run. Moon Ahin bristles. Jaeha, who names his own, wants hers back too.
Thirty-six husks lock into a porcelain wall, four deep, as the guards charge.
Shock batons crackle. The wall doesn't budge.
Everyone else drops onto the drain pipe below: rushing seawater, fifty metres above the pit floor.
Ho skids toward the edge. Jaeha grabs him, and Woo grabs Jaeha.
Pyo, slung over Borro's shoulder like a sack of rice, tries to keep his dignity. Briefly.
Jaeha leads at a run, shouting back the two rules of a wet half-pipe over a long drop.
Across the pit, the freight elevator drops fast: a squad in armour, and one slim figure with a crossbow.
Han Sora steps off like she owns the place, in Kanghan grey now, done pretending.
Her compass swings up toward the pipe, and she smiles like a bet just paid off.
Then her eyes find Lyra. The Director's shopping list just got longer.
Moon Ahin steps to the rim and plays the one card she has always had: her name.
It doesn't work. Director Baek has her down as home in bed, so this woman is nobody. Sora gives the order.
Moon Ahin goes white. The Director has already decided.
Stun bolts fly. Borro and Lyra flare into field form, full fighting strength, and Borro shields Moon Ahin from the volley.
Jaeha carries them both, taking part of every hit into himself. His shoulder bleeds again.
Moon Ahin stares at the shield that saved her. Borro doesn't look round. His Operator's rule covers everyone, even her.
Nib drops among the troopers in field form, kicking a shield aside as he lands, but nobody is carrying him.
Jaeha's limit is two. Tonight the scout bleeds alone, and Jaeha can only watch.
Lyra draws her white longbow to full, her braid lifting in the heat from the pit.
Two archers, two styles. Arrow and bolt meet in mid-air and burst apart.
Sora's next bolt pins Lyra's sleeve to the rock, with a compliment and an insult.
Lyra tears free, nocks two arrows at once, and returns the favour, word for word.
Two carbines go flying. Sora ducks a third arrow and comes up laughing.
A stun bolt hits Nib. His outline flickers like a dying bulb, and a baton rises over him.
Jaeha shifts his Carry from Lyra to Nib. The next baton blow lands in Jaeha, and Nib slips free.
But below them, the squad's wall of shields is outrunning the team to the hatch.
Pinned behind Borro's shield, Jaeha spots a red panel below and reads it the way he reads traps.
Flame, arrow, wave. Sprinklers overhead, bulkheads at each end. A fire here means a flood.
So he asks Lyra to start a fire. She stares at him. Jaeha has total faith in Kanghan's safety rules.
The arrow cracks a tank, and violet fire climbs the rack.
A horn blares, and a calm recorded voice starts a very short countdown.
The captain's men run for the exits. Sora looks up at the pipe, a fan for one moment.
The section floods, and the fire dies in steam. The squad is swept away, Nib leaps clear, and Sora dangles from the elevator, laughing.
She hauls herself up and slicks back her wet hair. She's enjoying this far too much.
Back at the balcony, the husk wall finally shatters.
Moon Ahin draws her baton back to her chest, a gesture she has never made. She's calling her husks home.
The pipe runs past the Tide Warden's chained left arm: a cliff of coral, its cuff as big as a house.
Her husks catch up, six fewer and some cracked, still in step. She counts every one.
She looks almost proud, and doesn't hide it fast enough.
Borro strains at a huge drain hatch, while the speakers send every guard to exactly where they're heading.
It swings open. A dark, dripping tunnel. The way out.
Then the water in the pipe trembles, and all three summons stop dead.
The Warden's eye opens: deep sea-green, ancient, and fully aware.
His huge head turns in its chains to look down at the three summons.
To Jaeha and Moon Ahin, it's only a hum that shakes the pipe. Jaeha shouts for his scout.
But the summons hear words in a language from home. He greets each by the place they come from.
Lyra is crying, her lips moving as if she knows the words.
The great eye above them is wet. He has called out to his own people for so long, and nobody answered.
Nib kneels in the water, fist on chest, the salute of the Ninth Wall. Borro bows his head.
Jaeha asks Nib to translate, and the scout's voice shakes. Four years waiting, and tonight three of his own walked in.
Behind them, torch beams bob closer down the pipe.
Then the eye turns to Jaeha and narrows, and the hum goes deeper.
Nib whispers the meaning. Somehow the giant knows what Jaeha does for his summons, and has pain of his own to give.
Everyone looks from the eye to Jaeha.
Jaeha pulls off his respirator and looks up into the eye, bare-faced. Then he does what he does best. He asks.
Far below, the chained hand slowly opens, palm up.
And the hero Kanghan has farmed for four years asks for one of two mercies: end him, or free him. Anything but this.
